citations.quote: The issue of whether a single family office is required to be licensed under the Ordinance is determined by reference to three key factors, all of which must be present in order to give rise to a licensing obligation: firstly, the services provided by the family office constitute one or more regulated activity as defined under the Ordinance; secondly, the family office is carrying on a business in the provision of such services; and thirdly, the business is carried on in Hong Kong.
What amounts to “carrying on a business in Hong Kong” is not defined in the Ordinance and will need to be determined by reference to the facts of each case

hypothesis.766b52cdba07b4437d5aaf15.distinction: Candidate interpretations considered are joint presence of all three factors, presence of any one factor, and attachment of “all” only within the regulated-activity factor. Only joint presence is defensible: “which” refers to “three key factors”, and the enumeration ends with “and thirdly”. “One or more” operates inside the first factor. There is no negation in the target clause. A necessity-only reading and an exhaustive-trigger reading differ over legal sufficiency, but yield the same Boolean for the selected antecedent.
